accepted.s: Ramakrishna Mission has its headquarters at which of the following places?
o: Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah
accepted.x: The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission is at Belur Math, situated on the Hooghly near Howrah.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the headquarters from the founder’s temple and other reform institutions.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s: The motto of the Ramakrishna Mission, ‘Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha’, signifies:
o: For one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world
accepted.x: The motto means ‘for one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world’.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive institutional motto rather than its general theme.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s:
Which of the following activities is associated with the practical work of the Ramakrishna Mission?
1. Running schools and colleges
2. Operating hospitals and orphanages
3. Providing famine and disaster relief
4. Promoting exclusively ritualistic worship
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Mission runs educational and medical institutions, orphanages and relief programmes. Its work is not exclusively ritualistic.
accepted.tq: Find the one extreme and incompatible statement among several practical-service activities.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the two broad components of the Ramakrishna Mission’s work?
o: A political party and a constitutional body engaged in legislative reform
A literary society and an educational department of the colonial government
A missionary organisation devoted exclusively to conversion and a trading corporation
A monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality, and lay disciples engaged in preaching and humanitarian work
accepted.x: The Mission combines a monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality with lay work involving preaching, philanthropy and humanitarian service.
accepted.tq: Compare the two institutional components and reject options that impose an exclusive or unrelated purpose.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s: The expression ‘daridra narayana’, associated with the practical Vedanta of the Ramakrishna Mission, refers to:
accepted.x: ‘Daridra narayana’ expresses the idea that service to the poor is service to God.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a service-oriented expression and the philosophical doctrines of the Theosophical Society.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa was associated with which of the following institutions?
o: Belur Math as its first President
accepted.x: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa served as a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple.
accepted.tq: Match the religious teacher with the institution directly associated with his life.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa is associated with the teaching:
o: As many faiths, so many paths
accepted.x: The statement ‘as many faiths, so many paths’ is associated with Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
accepted.tq: Identify the thinker through a characteristic teaching while avoiding slogans of unrelated movements.
accepted.sec: Ramakrishna Mission - founding year, place, founder, aims

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Swami Vivekananda:
1. His original name was Narendranath Datta.
2. He was born in Calcutta on 12 January 1863.
3. He was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
4. He was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta in Calcutta on 12 January 1863 and became Ramakrishna’s chief disciple. Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya was the birth name of Ramakrishna, not Vivekananda.
accepted.tq: Use the look-alike personal-name trap to separate the disciple’s name from the guru’s birth name.
accepted.sec: Vivekananda - original name, birth, books, National Youth Day

accepted.s: Swami Vivekananda’s birthday is observed in India as:
accepted.x: 12 January, the birthday of Swami Vivekananda, is observed as National Youth Day.
accepted.tq: Link the precise date-based observance with the correct national day.
accepted.sec: Vivekananda - original name, birth, books, National Youth Day

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: My Master was written by Swami Vivekananda. Annie Besant is not its author.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped author among otherwise correctly matched books and authors.
accepted.sec: Vivekananda - original name, birth, books, National Youth Day

accepted.s:
Which of the following books was written by Swami Vivekananda?
1. Karma Yoga
2. Raja Yoga
3. Jnana Yoga
4. Lectures from Colombo to Almora
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Karma Yoga, Raja Yoga, Jnana Yoga and Lectures from Colombo to Almora are all associated with Swami Vivekananda.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete author–works cluster rather than selecting only the most familiar title.
accepted.sec: Vivekananda - original name, birth, books, National Youth Day

accepted.s:
Swami Vivekananda is described by which of the following titles?
1. Prophet of Indian Nationalism
2. Maker of Modern India
3. Father of the Indian Constitution
4. Grand Old Man of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Vivekananda is described as the ‘Prophet of Indian Nationalism’ and the ‘Maker of Modern India’. The other titles refer to different personalities.
accepted.tq: Separate attributed titles from famous titles belonging to other national figures.
accepted.sec: Vivekananda - original name, birth, books, National Youth Day

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Vivekananda and the institutions connected with him in chronological order:
A. Founding of the Vedanta Society of New York
B. Establishment of Belur Math
C. Birth of Vivekananda
D. Death of Vivekananda
accepted.x: Vivekananda was born in 1863, founded the Vedanta Society of New York in 1894, Belur Math was established in 1898, and he died in 1902.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence by placing the dated personal event first and the two institutions before the death date.
accepted.sec: Institutions → founder

accepted.s: Which one of the following institutions was founded by Swami Vivekananda in New York in 1894?
accepted.x: The Vedanta Society of New York was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1894.
accepted.tq: Use founder–institution–year as a three-part identification clue.
accepted.sec: Institutions → founder

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Belur Math — Swami Vivekananda
2. Central Hindu College, Benaras — Annie Besant
3. Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle — Annie Besant
4. Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar — Swami Shraddhanand
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Belur Math was founded by Vivekananda; Annie Besant founded the two listed institutions, while Swami Shraddhanand founded Gurukul Kangri.
accepted.tq: Check each founder–institution pair independently before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Institutions → founder

accepted.s: The Central Hindu College at Benaras later became the nucleus of which institution?
accepted.x: The Central Hindu College founded by Annie Besant became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University in 1916, with Madan Mohan Malaviya.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an institutional precursor from similarly prominent universities.
accepted.sec: Institutions → founder

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Besant Theosophical College is correct?
o: It was founded at Lahore in 1886 and its first Principal was Hansraj.
It was founded at Haridwar in 1902 and its first Principal was Swami Shraddhanand.
It was founded at Adyar in 1882 and its first Principal was H.S. Olcott.
It was founded at Madanapalle in 1916 and its first Principal was H.J. Cousins.
accepted.x: The Besant Theosophical College was founded by Annie Besant at Madanapalle in 1916; H.J. Cousins was its first Principal.
accepted.tq: Use the founder, location, year and first office-holder together to defeat swapped institutional details.
accepted.sec: Institutions → founder

accepted.s: At Madanapalle, Rabindranath Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English under which title?
accepted.x: Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English at Madanapalle as ‘Morning Song of India’.
accepted.tq: Test the exact translated title rather than a plausible descriptive substitute.
accepted.sec: Institutions → founder

accepted.s:
With reference to the Theosophical Society, consider the following statements:
1. Its Indian headquarters is at Adyar.
2. The headquarters was shifted to Adyar in 1882.
3. Its original headquarters was established at Madras in 1875.
4. Its major beliefs included karma and reincarnation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Adyar became the Indian headquarters in 1882, and karma and reincarnation were among the Society’s beliefs. The Society was originally founded at New York, not Madras.
accepted.tq: Spot the location reversal between the original foundation and the later Indian headquarters.
accepted.sec: Theosophical Society - founders, first place, Indian HQ, leader

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a belief or objective associated with the Theosophical Society?
o: Exclusive propagation of one revealed religion
Study of ancient religions and philosophical traditions
accepted.x: The Theosophical Society promoted universal brotherhood and comparative study of religions; it did not advocate the exclusive propagation of one revealed religion.
accepted.tq: Reject the exclusive formulation when the organisation’s defining principle is comparative and universal.
accepted.sec: Theosophical Society - founders, first place, Indian HQ, leader

accepted.s:
The Theosophical Society drew upon which of the following Indian philosophical traditions?
1. Upanishads
2. Samkhya
3. Yoga
4. Vedanta
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Society drew upon the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete list of traditions rather than treating the Society as linked to only Vedanta.
accepted.sec: Theosophical Society - founders, first place, Indian HQ, leader

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Annie Besant is correct?
o: She came to India in 1882 and became President in 1893.
She joined the Society in 1907 and became President in 1916.
She founded the Society at New York in 1875 and became President in 1882.
She came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907.
accepted.x: Annie Besant came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907 after the death of Olcott.
accepted.tq: Separate the dates of joining, arrival in India and assumption of the presidency.
accepted.sec: Theosophical Society - founders, first place, Indian HQ, leader

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the social work of the Theosophical Society is correct?
1. It condemned child marriage.
2. It worked for the uplift of outcastes and widows.
3. It opposed the study of ancient religions.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Society condemned child marriage and worked for the uplift of outcastes and widows. It encouraged, rather than opposed, the study of ancient religions.
accepted.tq: Identify the false reversal of an organisation’s stated social and intellectual position.
accepted.sec: Theosophical Society - founders, first place, Indian HQ, leader

accepted.s: The Telugu name of the Theosophical Society is:
accepted.x: The Theosophical Society is known in Telugu as Divya Gnana Samajam.
accepted.tq: Test the exact regional-language equivalent of a well-known organisation.

accepted.s: At the Parliament of the World’s Religions held at Chicago, which participant represented Jainism?
accepted.x: Virchand Gandhi represented Jainism at the Chicago Parliament of Religions. P.C. Mozoomdar represented the Brahmo Samaj, while Anagarika Dharmapala represented Buddhism from Ceylon.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the participants by their religious traditions rather than by the common event.
accepted.sec: Chicago Parliament of Religions - year, Indian participants

 d. Swami Vivekananda
